guide.bandsIntro: Your writing performance is mapped to the Canadian Language Benchmarks (CLB) — NCLC in French. Here is how the benchmarks line up with the CEFR levels used in most French courses:
guide.bandsNote: Equivalencies are approximate and for guidance only. Always confirm the exact requirement for your immigration program with official sources.
guide.clb4: Basic, simple sentences with frequent errors.
guide.clb5: Connected text, limited range, basic connectors.
guide.clb7: Clear arguments, varied connectors, few errors — the common PR target.
guide.closing: This guide is for preparation purposes and is not affiliated with the official TEF or TCF exam bodies. Scores and levels mentioned are estimates to help guide your study; your official exam result may differ.
guide.ctaBody: Write on a real task, and our AI returns your errors by category, corrections, and an estimated CLB level in seconds.

guide.docDesc: A complete guide to the TEF and TCF Canada writing exam: the three tâches, word counts, CLB 7 score equivalency, common mistakes, and how to prepare to reach CLB 7 (CEFR B2) and beyond.
guide.docTitle: TEF / TCF Canada Writing Guide: How to Reach CLB 7 | prepfrancais
guide.faq1a: Both the TEF Canada and TCF Canada assess French writing for Canadian immigration. Each has a written-expression section built around short, practical tasks. The TCF Canada writing section has three tasks (tâches) of increasing length and difficulty; the TEF Canada is similar in spirit. Both map results to the Canadian Language Benchmarks (CLB / NCLC).
guide.faq1q: What is the difference between the TEF and TCF Canada writing exam?
guide.faq2a: Many Express Entry candidates aim for CLB 7 in each skill, which corresponds roughly to CEFR B2. CLB 7 is a common threshold for maximising points, but exact requirements depend on your immigration program. Always check the current official requirement for your specific program.
guide.faq2q: What CLB level do I need for Canadian PR?
guide.faq3a: The writing section typically lasts about 60 minutes across the tasks. A common split is roughly 10 minutes for the short message, 20 minutes for the narrative/article, and 30 minutes for the argumentative comparison — though you manage the total time yourself.
guide.faq3q: How long is the TEF/TCF writing section?
guide.faq4a: A typical guide is 60–120 words for Tâche 1 (short message), 120–150 words for Tâche 2 (article/narrative), and 120–180 words for Tâche 3 (compare two opinions). Staying within the range matters: too short loses content marks, too long wastes time and risks errors.
guide.faq4q: How many words should I write for each task?
guide.faq5a: Focus on the errors that cap your level: gender/agreement, verb conjugation, prepositions and anglicisms. Learn a small set of higher-level connectors, practise to a timer, and get feedback on every piece you write so you stop repeating the same mistakes. Consistent, corrected practice moves scores faster than writing without feedback.
guide.faq5q: How can I improve my French writing score quickly?
guide.faq6a: An AI checker gives instant, consistent feedback on grammar, vocabulary, structure and an estimated level, which is useful for regular practice between formal mock exams. It is a preparation aid, not the official exam — estimated scores guide your study but your real result may differ.
guide.faq6q: Is an AI writing checker accurate for TEF/TCF preparation?
guide.heroSub: Everything you need to understand the French writing exam for Canadian immigration — the three tâches, how many words to write, what CLB 7 really means, the mistakes that cap your score, and how to prepare efficiently.
guide.intro: The TEF Canada and TCF Canada are the two French exams accepted for Canadian immigration. For most candidates, the goal in writing (expression écrite) is to reach CLB 7, which corresponds roughly to CEFR B2 and is a common threshold for maximising Express Entry points. This guide explains exactly what the writing section asks of you and how to prepare for it.
guide.mistake1: Wrong article or adjective agreement (le/la, accord). Learn nouns with their article and make adjectives agree.
guide.mistake2: Tense and auxiliary errors, especially passé composé (être vs avoir) and the subjunctive.
guide.mistake3: Wrong verb + preposition pairs (penser à, dépendre de) and place prepositions (à, en, au).
guide.mistake4: False friends like “actuellement” (currently) or calques from English structures.
guide.mistake5: Overusing “et / mais”. At CLB 7+ use “cependant, néanmoins, par conséquent, dans la mesure où”.
guide.mistake6: Going under or over the word count, or running out of time on Tâche 3.
guide.mistakesIntro: At CLB 7, examiners expect clear structure and only occasional errors. These six categories are where most candidates lose marks — fixing them is the fastest way to move up a band:
guide.mistakesTitle: The mistakes that cap your score
guide.t1desc: A short, practical message: an invitation, a request, an apology or a note to a friend, colleague or service. Examiners look for the right register, a clear purpose and correct everyday vocabulary.
guide.t2desc: A narrative or descriptive text — often a blog post or article recounting an experience. You are expected to organise ideas, use connectors and vary your vocabulary and tenses.
guide.t3desc: An argumentative text comparing two opinions on a social topic, then defending your own. This is where higher scores are won or lost: clear structure, nuanced connectors and an explicit point of view.
guide.tachesIntro: The writing section is built around three tasks of increasing length and difficulty. You manage your own time across them — roughly 60 minutes in total.
guide.tip1: Practise to a timer so the 60-minute limit feels normal, not stressful.
guide.tip2: Write on all three task types regularly — not just the one you find easiest.
guide.tip3: Get feedback on every piece, so you stop repeating the same mistakes.
guide.tip4: Build a personal list of higher-level connectors and reuse them deliberately.
guide.tip5: Read model answers at CLB 7+ to internalise structure and register.

privacy.intro: prepfrancais helps you prepare for the TEF and TCF Canada exams. To do that it stores what you write and say, because reviewing your own mistakes is the whole point of the product. This page says exactly what is kept, why, and how to get rid of it.
privacy.p1: Your name and email address, set when you register. A password, stored only as a bcrypt hash — nobody at prepfrancais can read it. The French you submit for correction: essays, pasted text, and the transcripts of your spoken answers. The corrections themselves, including every error found and the CEFR level awarded. Your practice history: streaks, XP, badges, review results and the timezone used to bucket them.
privacy.p2: A speaking answer is sent to a transcription provider, turned into text, and the text is what we store. The audio itself is not written to our database or kept on our servers after the transcript comes back.
privacy.p3: Your text or transcript is sent to the AI provider that grades it — currently one of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Groq or DeepSeek, and one of OpenAI, Google, Groq or AssemblyAI for transcription. They process it to produce the correction. We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with advertisers.
privacy.p4: For as long as your account exists, because your mistake history is what the review games are built from. Delete your account and the submissions, mistakes and review sessions attached to it go with it.
privacy.p5: You can ask for a copy of everything held about you, ask for corrections, or ask for the account and its contents to be deleted. Write to the address below and we will act on it within 30 days. If you are in Quebec, Law 25 gives you these rights explicitly; elsewhere in Canada, PIPEDA does.
privacy.p6: Two httpOnly cookies keep you signed in, plus one ordinary cookie that only records that a session exists so the app can skip a pointless request when you are signed out. Your language choice is kept in local storage. There is no advertising or cross-site tracking, so there is nothing here to consent to.
privacy.p7: Questions or requests about your data: {{email}}

refund.intro: prepfrancais sells access to a digital service. This page says exactly when a plan can be cancelled, when it can be refunded, how to ask, and how long the money takes to come back.
refund.p1: A plan is timed access to the paid features — AI writing corrections, AI speaking evaluations, the exam simulator and the study packs — for the length printed on the plan you chose. Access is applied to your account as soon as the payment is confirmed. Nothing physical is sold and nothing is shipped.
refund.p2: You can cancel at any time and there is no cancellation fee. Write to {{email}} from the address on your account and we cancel the mandate, which stops every future charge. Cancelling does not cut short what you have already paid for: access runs to the end of the period and then returns to the free plan. Your account, your history and your saved mistakes are kept.
refund.p3: Within 7 days of a payment, if none of the AI corrections or speaking evaluations that plan gave you have been used, we refund it in full and you do not have to give a reason. Ask inside those 7 days and we will not argue about it.
refund.p4: Once an AI correction or a speaking evaluation from the plan has been delivered, the plan counts as delivered and is no longer refundable, and the same applies once the 7 days have passed. This does not cover a failure on our side — that is the next clause.
refund.p5: If a correction fails because an AI provider was unavailable, the attempt returns to your balance automatically: you are never charged for work that was not delivered. Beyond that, if a payment was taken twice, if access was never unlocked after a successful payment, or if the service was unusable for a meaningful part of your plan, we refund in full whatever the 7 days say. Tell us and we will put it right.
refund.p6: An approved refund goes back to the card or account the payment came from — we cannot send it anywhere else. We instruct it within 3 business days of approving it. Your bank then takes its own time: usually 5 to 7 business days, and up to 10 for an international card.
refund.p7: Plans are charged in the currency shown on the pricing page, with the payment processing fee itemised there before you pay. A refund returns the amount we charged. Any cross-border, foreign-exchange or issuer fee your own bank added is charged by your bank and not by us, so we cannot return it, and an exchange rate that has moved between the payment and the refund can change what finally lands in your account.
refund.p8: Email {{email}} from the address on your account, with the invoice number from your receipt or the date and amount of the payment. We reply within two business days and tell you plainly whether it is approved, and why.

shipping.intro: prepfrancais is a digital service. Nothing is posted, couriered or shipped, and there is no delivery charge. This page explains how access reaches you instead, and how quickly.
shipping.p1: There is no physical product. We do not post books, discs or printed material, so there is no shipping address to give us, no delivery fee, and no tracking number.
shipping.p2: Everything is delivered inside your account at prepfrancais.com. When a payment is confirmed, the plan is applied to the account that paid and the paid features unlock immediately — normally within a minute or two, and within 24 hours at the outside if a payment needs manual confirmation. There is nothing to download and nothing to install: sign in and it is there.
shipping.p3: An invoice is emailed to the address on your account as soon as the payment lands, and the same receipts stay in your account under Invoices for as long as the account exists.
shipping.p4: Everywhere. The service works from anywhere with an internet connection and there is no country we exclude.
shipping.p5: If a payment succeeded and the paid features are still locked, sign out and back in first — that refreshes what your browser knows about the account. If it is still locked, email {{email}} with the date and amount of the payment and we will unlock it, usually the same business day. If we cannot deliver it at all, we refund it in full.

terms.intro: Plain terms for using prepfrancais. Using the service means you accept them.
terms.p1: prepfrancais is preparation software. It grades your French with an AI model against the TCF Canada format and explains what it found. It is not affiliated with France Éducation international, the CIEP, or any official TEF or TCF examiner.
terms.p2: The CEFR level we return is an estimate produced by a language model. It is useful for tracking progress and finding weaknesses. It is not an official result, it does not predict your exam score, and it cannot be submitted anywhere as proof of proficiency.
terms.p3: One account per person. Keep your password to yourself; you are responsible for what happens under your account. Tell us if you think someone else has access.
terms.p4: Free accounts get a one-time trial of 3 AI writing corrections and 3 speaking evaluations, of which one may be the tâche 2 roleplay, plus a small monthly allowance for open-ended conversation practice. If a correction fails because the AI provider is unavailable, the attempt is returned automatically — you are never charged for work that was not delivered.
terms.p5: prepfrancais sells timed access plans to the paid features. The price, the plan length and the payment processing fee are all shown on the pricing page before you pay, and the payment itself is taken by our payment provider — card details never reach our servers. A plan renews until you cancel it, and you can cancel at any time at no charge. What can be refunded, and how long it takes, is set out in the refund and cancellation policy; how access reaches you is set out in the delivery policy.
terms.p6: What you write stays yours. You grant us only the permission needed to run it through grading and show you the result. We do not publish it, and we do not use it to train models.
terms.p7: Do not scrape the exam material, resell access, or automate submissions. Rate limits apply and accounts that abuse them can be suspended.
terms.p8: The service is provided as is. We work hard to keep grading accurate and available, but we cannot be liable for exam outcomes, missed sittings, or decisions taken on the basis of a practice score.
